sections.h2: Does Iowa have an estate tax or an inheritance tax today?
sections.html:
Iowa has neither one for a person who dies now. The state estate tax stopped applying to deaths on or after January 1, 2005, and the inheritance tax stopped applying to deaths on or after January 1, 2025, according to the Iowa Department of Revenue.

The two taxes work differently, and heirs often mix them up. An estate tax is charged on the whole estate. Iowa's inheritance tax was based on what each beneficiary had a right to receive, which is why the rate depended on who the heir was.

For anyone who inherits an Iowa house now, the practical result is simple: no Iowa death tax return stands between the heirs and a sale. Other costs still apply, and the sections below cover them.

sections.h2: How was the Iowa inheritance tax phased out?
sections.html:
The Legislature cut the tax in steps over four years and then ended it. Under Iowa Code 450.10(7), the normal rates were reduced by a set percentage depending on the year of death.

Year of deathRate reduction
202120 percent
202240 percent
202360 percent
202480 percent
2025 and laterChapter does not apply

The end point is written into chapter 450, which says it does not apply to property of estates of decedents dying on or after January 1, 2025. The tax on unknown heirs was cut on the same schedule and ended for 2025 deaths too.

If the person who owned the house died in 2024 or earlier, the old rules can still matter, so keep reading.

sections.h2: Who paid inheritance tax before 2025, and who was exempt?
sections.html:
Close family paid nothing. Property passing to a surviving spouse, parents and grandparents, children, stepchildren, grandchildren and other lineal descendants was exempt under chapter 450.

Everyone else could owe tax, and the rate climbed with the amount received. The statute set these brackets before the phase-down reductions:

  • Siblings, sons-in-law and daughters-in-law: 5 percent on the first $12,500, rising by bracket to 10 percent on amounts above $150,000.
  • Other heirs, such as nieces, nephews, cousins and friends: 10 percent up to $50,000, 12 percent to $100,000 and 15 percent above that.
  • Out-of-state charitable bodies: 10 percent on the full amount.
  • For-profit firms and corporations: 15 percent on the full amount.

Some transfers were left out altogether. An estate of $25,000 or less after debts owed no tax, tangible personal property was exempt when the total was $5,000 or less, and gifts to qualifying charitable, educational and religious groups were excluded.

sections.h2: What deadlines applied to an Iowa inheritance tax return?
sections.html:
The tax came due on the last day of the ninth month after the date of death, and the return was due the same day unless none was required. The Department's own page says the beneficiary was responsible for the tax on earlier deaths.

The Department of Revenue could extend payment for up to ten years from the end of the month of death to avoid hardship, but interest ran from the original date. Late payment also carried a penalty.

These dates only matter now for an older death. A house inherited from someone who died in, say, 2023 can still carry an open file, which is worth checking before closing.

sections.h2: Can an old inheritance tax lien still affect selling an inherited Iowa house?
sections.html:
It can, for deaths before 2025. Under Iowa Code 450.7, the tax was a lien on the taxable estate and the decedent's property from the date of death until paid, and a sale did not wipe it out.

The same section says the lien generally ends ten years after death, and it ranks ahead of later mortgages, buyers and judgment creditors without any recorded notice. Property passing to a spouse, parents, children and other lineal descendants was never subject to the lien.

Ways the lien was released or cleared:

  • Filing a receipt showing the tax was paid with the clerk of court.
  • Filing a certificate that no tax was owed.
  • Filing a release or waiver.
  • Where no return was required, filing an affidavit describing the real estate in the county where it sits (section 450.22).

A title company or estate attorney normally handles this paperwork. If you are an heir selling a house from a pre-2025 death, ask them whether anything is still open of record.

sections.h2: Does the federal estate tax reach an Iowa house?
sections.html:
Only for very large estates. The IRS lists a filing threshold of $15,000,000 for deaths in 2026 and $13,990,000 for 2025, as shown on its estate tax page.

An estate must file a federal return when the gross estate, plus adjusted taxable gifts and the specific gift tax exemption, goes above that figure. A surviving spouse can also elect to carry over the unused exemption of the person who died. That election is made on a timely filed estate tax return.

Most Iowa families who inherit a house will fall far below the threshold. The house is one asset among others in that total, and a sale price does not by itself trigger a filing.

sections.h2: What property taxes still follow an inherited Iowa home?
sections.html:
Ordinary property tax continues whether or not anyone owes a death tax. Iowa counties bill in two installments, and the first becomes delinquent on October 1 and the second on April 1, under Iowa Code 445.37. If the last day of September or March falls on a weekend, delinquency moves to the second business day of the next month.

Heirs sometimes assume the homestead benefit passes along with the house. It does not run on its own. The Des Moines County assessor explains that once a person qualifies, the exemption continues until the property is sold or the owner no longer qualifies, so an heir who will not live there may be taxed without it. Our Iowa homestead exemption guide covers the 2026 change.

Plan for the taxes due on the estate's calendar. A cash buyer can usually close ahead of an installment date, and the settlement figures show what is paid from proceeds.

sections.h2: What does selling an inherited house in Iowa involve now?
sections.html:
The steps depend on how title is held and on whether a court-supervised estate is open. If the owner died with a will or without one, the person with authority over the estate signs the deed, and the buyer's title company will ask for proof of that authority.

Recording the deed also triggers the Iowa transfer tax, set by Iowa Code 428A.1 at eighty cents for each $500 of value above the first $500. It is paid to the county recorder, and a declaration of value goes in with the deed. Transfers with no consideration are not taxed.

  • Gather the death certificate and any will.
  • Confirm who has authority to sell, whether an executor or heirs holding title.
  • Ask the title company to search for liens, including any pre-2025 inheritance tax lien.
  • Check which property tax installment is next.

We buy inherited Iowa houses as they stand, which helps when the home needs repairs the heirs would rather not fund.

faqs.q: Is there an inheritance tax in Iowa in 2026?
faqs.a: No. Iowa's Department of Revenue states that the inheritance tax does not apply to deaths occurring on or after January 1, 2025, so a 2026 death creates no Iowa inheritance tax return.

faqs.q: Does Iowa have a state estate tax?
faqs.a: No. The Iowa estate tax does not apply to deaths on or after January 1, 2005. The federal estate tax is separate and has a 2026 filing threshold of $15,000,000.

faqs.q: Do I owe Iowa inheritance tax if my parent died in 2024?
faqs.a: A child inheriting from a parent owed nothing, because property passing to children and other lineal descendants was exempt under chapter 450. Siblings and other heirs could owe a tax at rates reduced by 80 percent for 2024 deaths.

faqs.q: Can an inheritance tax lien block a sale of the house?
faqs.a: It can for older deaths. The lien under section 450.7 generally ends ten years after death, but it can be released earlier by a receipt, certificate or waiver, and a title company can tell you whether one is on record.

faqs.q: Who pays the Iowa transfer tax when an inherited house is sold?
faqs.a: Settle that point in the purchase contract with your title company.

faqs.q: Do heirs keep the homestead exemption on an inherited Iowa house?
faqs.a: Not automatically. County assessors say the exemption continues only while the owner still qualifies, and it ends when the property is sold.
